ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Emily Dickinson

code.originalText: Three-week kidney and blood pressure review in the clinic, combined with nephrology consultation and kidney ultrasound on one trip

text.paragraph: Three-week kidney and blood pressure review; nephrology consultation and kidney ultrasound on the same trip. [S]

Ms. Dickinson comes to the clinic for the first time in two years, on a quiet early appointment that combines this review, a kidney ultrasound, and her nephrology consultation so that she makes one trip. She started losartan 50 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg, and vitamin D3 three weeks ago and stopped naproxen. Her headaches are less frequent, about twice a week, and she takes acetaminophen for them. The morning nausea has eased. She has had no lightheadedness, cough, or muscle aches. Her home blood pressure averages 150/90 on her own upper-arm cuff, which read within 4 mmHg of the clinic device today. She has cut down on salted foods. She saw Dr. Adeyemi of nephrology this morning after the ultrasound. [S]

list.item:
Chronic kidney disease G3a A2 (N18.31). Three weeks after starting losartan, potassium 4.6 mmol/L and creatinine 1.26 mg/dL (eGFR 51, a 5 percent rise in creatinine), well within the accepted rise. A second urine albumin-creatinine ratio of 262 mg/g confirms persistent A2 albuminuria. Ultrasound shows normal-sized kidneys with mildly increased echogenicity and no obstruction. Nephrology agrees that hypertensive kidney disease is the probable cause and that no biopsy is needed. [S]
Increase losartan to 100 mg daily.
Start dapagliflozin 10 mg daily, as nephrology advised.
Potassium and creatinine in four weeks, drawn at home by the mobile phlebotomy service, with a video visit the same day.
Sick-day rules explained: pause losartan and dapagliflozin during vomiting, diarrhea, or poor intake, and call.

Hypertension with chronic kidney disease (I12.9). 148/88 mmHg in the clinic and 150/90 at home, improving but above the KDIGO systolic target of below 120. [S]
Losartan increase as above; continue home readings and send them weekly.

Vitamin D deficiency (E55.9). Taking vitamin D3 daily. [S]
Recheck 25-hydroxyvitamin D, calcium, phosphate, and PTH at six to twelve months.
